one_liner: Portable Linux build of NetBSD's widechar curses; builds 6.6x faster and installs far smaller than ncurses, with no runtime benchmark.
what_it_does: A port of NetBSD's libcurses, libterminfo, libpanel, libmenu and libform plus tic, tput, tset, infocmp and tabs to Linux (developed on musl-based sabotage Linux, also builds on glibc). It implements the curses API with wide-character support, so most ncursesw programs compile unchanged once linked with -lcurses -lterminfo (pkg-config .pc files are installed). It is source-compatible, not ABI-compatible: struct layouts differ and a few ncurses extensions are absent.
how_it_is_fast: The win is build time and footprint, not screen-update speed. There is no autoconf configure step (settings are plain make variables or config.mak) and the whole tree is one non-recursive GNUmakefile that parallelises fully, with only a few small sh/awk generator steps, versus ncurses' configure script and its layers of awk/sed/cpp preprocessing; the source is about 3.3 MB against 15.8 MB. Terminfo is compiled into a CDB constant database with perfect-hash tables generated at build time by the bundled nbperf tool, and a dozen common terminals are compiled into the library.
when_to_use: Source-based or embedded Linux distributions (especially musl) where ncurses is an early bootstrap dependency and its 59 s configure-heavy build and 15.9 MB install matter.
Static or size-constrained builds of curses applications: a static nano linked against it was 288 KB versus 334 KB with ncurses in the README test.
Cross-compiling curses apps: no configure script or ncurses5-config tool to fight, HOSTCC selects cross mode, and pkg-config files are provided.
Projects that want a small, readable BSD-licensed curses codebase to patch or vendor.
when_not_to_use: When you expect faster terminal rendering: no runtime comparison against ncurses exists in the repo or in public sources found.
Applications that need mouse input (ncurses mouse calls are no-op macros), more than 510 color pairs, or rarely used functions such as vidputs() and wgetscrreg() (issue #60).
Programs or bindings that touch ncurses struct members or expect libncursesw's ABI, such as Python's curses module, which needs a patch.
Unicode-heavy UIs until open issue #53 is resolved: a reporter found wide characters printed after initscr() rendering as question marks, with no maintainer reply.
Projects needing an actively maintained library: last release v0.3.2 (2021-05-20), last commit 2024-01-16, and several open issues have no response.

integration.form: static lib and shared lib (both built by 'make all')
integration.dependencies: none at runtime beyond libc; build needs GNU make, a POSIX sh, awk and a C compiler (a host compiler too when cross-compiling); no configure script
integration.min_toolchain: GNU make and a C compiler; C standard version not documented; builds against musl and glibc
integration.platforms: Linux (musl, glibc) on any architecture; README says other POSIX systems should work with minor changes
integration.thread_safety: not documented (the README says nothing about threads); treat as single-threaded like classic curses
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — source-compatible for most ncursesw programs after linking -lcurses -lterminfo (static and shared libs are both built), but not ABI-compatible, mouse calls are no-ops, some functions are missing, and code that reads ncurses internals needs patches

gotchas: Footprint rows are not like for like: the 15.9 MB vs 1.3 MB installed size excludes netbsd curses' manpages and terminfo database but counts ncurses' (1.1 MB and 6.4 MB), and the shared-library row compares libncursesw.so with a library that is split into libcurses and libterminfo without saying whether libterminfo.so is counted; the current install target also installs manpages, so a rerun would not reproduce 1.3 MB.

Terminfo is a CDB file, not the ncurses directory tree: only about a dozen terminals are built in, others need 'make terminfo/terminfo.cdb' installed to $PREFIX/share/terminfo.cdb or ~/.terminfo.cdb, and newer terminals can be missing (issue #54 asks for foot; a GNU screen lookup fix landed only in January 2024).
Functions such as tgetent() and tputs() live in libterminfo, so autoconf checks that only try -lcurses or -lncurses can fail until LIBS='-lcurses -lterminfo' is passed.
Open display bugs without maintainer response: #53 (wide characters after initscr() shown as '?'), #59 (garbled display after running vis in st) and #28 (sl hangs in the Linux console).
pick_this_over_siblings_when: The only catalogued sibling, micron.cpp, replaces memcpy/memset/memmove and does not overlap; pick netbsd-curses when the goal is a smaller, faster-to-build curses implementation for a distro or static binary.
verified_claims_summary: One first-party run from the 2016-era README (Table 1, Appendix A): on an unnamed dual-core x86_64 sabotage Linux system with -Os size-optimised CFLAGS and unstated compiler and library versions, make -j2 all install took 59 s for ncurses and 9 s for netbsd curses (6.6x, derived from page data), libncursesw.so was 346 KB vs 150 KB and a static nano 334 KB vs 288 KB (1.16x); there is no benchmark script and no runtime (rendering or input) measurement.
status_note: Stale: last release v0.3.2 on 2021-05-20 and last commit 2024-01-16, with open bug reports unanswered, but it is BSD-2/3-Clause, has no runtime dependencies and is small enough to vendor; it remains sabotage Linux's curses.
